title: test experiment selection: resolve an existing experiment by name and activate it by ID instead of calling set_experiment by name
answers: Why does my compatibility test write its evaluation run to the Default experiment instead of the one from the older version?
Why does mlflow.set_experiment by name create a new experiment with the ./mlruns fallback location?
How do I make a test fail fast when the expected experiment is missing?
body:
Path: tests/test_mlflow_version_comp.py:test_mlflow_2_x_comp, which reopens a tracking database written by MLflow 2.x and runs the 3.x check_evaluate and check_load steps against it.
Rule: To use an experiment that a previous step created, call mlflow.get_experiment_by_name(name), assert it is not None, and then call mlflow.set_experiment(experiment_id=experiment.experiment_id). Do not call mlflow.set_experiment(name) to reuse it: when the name is not found, set_experiment creates a new experiment, and that experiment falls back to the ./mlruns artifact location.
Symptom: The evaluation run was logged into the Default experiment, not the 2.x-created experiment, and artifacts were written under the shared ./mlruns directory.
Constraints: Applies when a test must activate an experiment it did not create in the same step. For experiments the test creates itself, pass an explicit artifact_location as well.
applies: Tests that switch the active experiment across MLflow versions or after reopening a tracking store.
says: Compatibility test logs its evaluation run into the Default experiment instead of the older one
Set experiment by name creates a new experiment in the mlruns fallback location
Compatibility test should reuse an experiment from the 2.x run by ID
Test should fail fast when the expected experiment is missing
search: In the 2.x-to-3.x compatibility test, reuse an existing experiment by looking it up by name, asserting it exists, and activating it by ID rather than calling set_experiment by name. set_experiment by name creates a new experiment with the ./mlruns fallback when not found. For self-created experiments, also pass an explicit artifact location.
